data.name: Sipun
data.gender_notes: Sipun is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is the lord and controller of all water sources and rivers, bringing calmness and strength. The name Sipun carries the meaning “Lord of Water” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sipun usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of water and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a boy symbolizing the power of water and the calming effect it has on our emotions and spirit.
data.etymology: Sipun belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Water.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sipun total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Sipun" holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism as it refers to the Lord of all water sources and rivers. The name pays homage to this power of water that sustains life and provides a source of calmness and strength.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Sipun" also carries deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. It reflects the belief in the divine presence of the Lord in all aspects of the natural world. By adopting this name, one acknowledges the innate connection between oneself and the divine, and recognizes the importance of respecting and honoring the gifts of nature that sustain and nourish us. It also serves as a reminder that just as rivers bring life and support civilizations, our own lives should similarly bring joy, peace, and prosperity to others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sipun, meaning "a vessel of purity," signifies an individual who is devoted to preserving and disseminating the sacred knowledge, much like a vessel holds and carries water. This name imbues its bearer with a sense of duty towards spiritual growth and the upliftment of others.

historical_references.reference: The name Sipun is mentioned in the ancient Hindu epic Mahabharata, in the context of the Kurukshetra war. Sipun was a powerful and brave warrior, a kshatriya, who was a descendant of the Lunar Dynasty. He was a friend and ally of the Pandava brother Bhima and fought on their side during the war.

Another reference to Sipun can be found in the Puranic texts, specifically in the Agni Purana. In this context, Sipun is mentioned as a great ascetic and devotee of Lord Shiva. He is said to have performed severe penances and gained the grace of the god, who appeared before him and blessed him.
